title: OpenHydroLab: interactive, physics-accurate animations for teaching hydraulics and hydrology
description:
OpenHydroLab is an open-source suite of eight interactive browser laboratories for teaching undergraduate hydraulics and hydrology. Each module is a self-contained HTML page that computes every displayed quantity live from the governing equation and runs offline from a local file, with no installation and no third-party host.

Modules: channel geometry and the Froude number, Manning uniform flow, specific energy and choking, hydraulic jumps, gradually varied flow profiles, storm hydrographs, the unit hydrograph workbench, and an IDF/frequency-analysis pipeline on a real 27-year gauge record.

Release 1.0.0 adds the verification harness: 405 automated tests yielding 354 numerical comparisons across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, against reference values derived independently of the code. The verification protocol is documented in validation/validation-protocol.md and the generated dataset in validation/results/. This protocol establishes computational fidelity and reproducibility only; it makes no claim about learning outcomes.
